sensors.name: light sensor LLIGHT (the light falling on the robot from above)

functions: followLine (b4): reads LLIGHT and curves left below 50 %, else curves right
control_flow: followLine: if the light from above on its left is below 50 %, curve left; otherwise curve right; then return.
The curves are without a distance, so the robot keeps curving until the next movement block, and the loop reads the light again at once.

decision_points.condition: the light falling on the robot from above on its left (LLIGHT) is below 50 %

branches.outcome: the light is below 50 % (dim, deep inside a tunnel): it curves left
the light is 50 % or more (bright, in the open): it curves right

input_dimensions.dimension: the light falling on the robot from above

equivalence_classes: dim light, deep inside a tunnel
input_dimensions.dimension: the light falling on the robot from above

scenarios.coded_response: The light is bright, so it curves right again and again: it circles, and the line on the floor makes no difference to it
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line, in the open, so the light from above is bright
scenarios.trigger: The program runs and reads the light from above again and again
scenarios.title: Follows the line in the open
assumptions: The end of the line is where the robot should get to.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the black line to its end

scenarios.coded_response: The light is dim, so it curves left again and again: it circles in the tunnel, and the line on the floor makes no difference to it
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line deep inside a tunnel, so the light from above is dim
scenarios.trigger: The program runs and reads the light from above again and again
scenarios.title: Follows the line through a dark tunnel
assumptions: 'Follow the line' also holds where the line runs through a dark tunnel.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the black line through the tunnel to its end

uncertainties: Your program reads the light from above, not the line tracker, so a line on the floor changes nothing for it and it cannot follow one.
You didn't say where the line ends, nor what the robot should do in a dark tunnel: the tunnel scenario takes 'follow the line' to apply there too.
In bright light the program circles to the right, so it moves away from a line instead of along it.

planned: Follows the line out of the dark tunnel

outcomes.words: the condition doesn't hold: the else part runs
planned: In the open, it follows the line to the goal

worlds.name: A line to its end in the open

tests.name: In the open, it follows the line to the goal
tests.scenario: Given the robot starts on a black line in bright light, when the program runs, then it follows the line and reaches Goal 1 at its end.

equivalence_partitions.dimension: the light falling on the robot from above

expected_results: It follows the black line and reaches Goal 1 at the line's end.

assumptions: The end of the line is where it should get to.

tests.reason: You said the robot should follow the line; this checks it gets to the line's end in the open.
